thread:
alex_cust: Hi team — we flipped a few test services to the free plan this morning and started seeing intermittent 429s and a couple of 401s. Traffic is small (dev pods), but errors started around 09:40 UTC. Any chance of a temporary bridge while we sort billing?
sarah_support: sorry you're hitting that, alex. can you paste the `x-request-id` from one of the 429 responses and the API key suffix? also, which endpoint — /v1/chat or /v1/generate?
alex_cust: root key suffix is ...-9f3, endpoint is /v1/chat, client logs attached (stack trace not huge). example response header: `x-request-id: 01HXYGZ7-abc`, `x-ratelimit-limit: 60`, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `x-ratelimit-reset: 1680003456`
sarah_support: thanks. looks like you hit the per-minute cap — free-tier is more strict for concurrency. two quick notes: 1) if multiple pods share the same key they combine into the same quota bucket, 2) we can offer a short-term grace for small internal dev teams while you finalize billing.
ben_sales: pinging in — we can provision a temporary "tier bridge" (24h grace window, +50k tokens) for accounts qualifying for dev testing. need account id and invoice contact. if they want a longer bump we'll move to a paid trial with a small cc capture.
alex_cust: account id: acct_72H4. invoice contact is me (alex@acme.dev). small team, likely light 5-10 rps spikes while CI runs. 401s were odd — we rotated keys right before this incident.
mike_infra: two things on the 401: if you rotated keys, make sure no sidecar or old process is retrying with the revoked key — that will show as 401 until the old process stops. also check for trailing whitespace in the header (we've seen that cause intermittent 401s with some HTTP libs).
katy_ops: noted. alex, can you run a quick curl against /v1/auth/check? example:```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-...-9f3" https://api.redwood.example/v1/auth/check
```
should return 200 + account id. if it returns 401 we can rule out rotation issues.
alex_cust: ran it, returning 200. so rotation looks fine. logs show retries from a legacy CI runner that didn't pick up env change — stopping that now. 429s still happening occasionally.
sarah_support: ok good call on the runner. for the 429s, two config paths: 1) we can suggest changing to per-worker keys (one key per pod) so quotas are isolated, 2) enable our short-term dev burst (temp grace). which do you prefer?
alex_cust: per-worker keys would be better long-term, but it's a bit of work in our infra. would appreciate the grace while we migrate. how quickly can it be added?
ben_sales: I can approve a 24h bridge immediately once I have a written confirmation from the invoice contact. it adds +50k tokens and relaxes the per-minute cap from 60 to 300 for the bridge window. no charge, single-use. can we confirm?
alex_cust: confirmed, please enable.
ben_sales: accepted. enabling now, will post when applied.
quota-bot: [system] Temporary quota adjustment applied to acct_72H4: +50000 tokens, per-minute rate limit changed to 300 for 24h (expires 1845765301).
alex_cust: I can confirm 429s have dropped to zero in the last 8 minutes. thank you. one more question — will this affect billing or usage history so we can export a clean report later?
sarah_support: the grace is non-billable and annotated in usage logs as `dev_tier_bridge`. you'll see an entry in the usage export and we can strip it for accounting if needed.
mike_infra: long-term, recommend moving to one of these approaches: - per-pod key rotation (isolates quota), - client-side exponential backoff + jitter, - local request queueing to keep effective rps steady. if you want, we can share a small snippet for the client-side throttler.
katy_ops: also add a background job to detect 429s and pause CI runners briefly — saved a few teams elsewhere.
alex_cust: would take the throttler snippet. and any docs on creating per-pod keys programmatically?
sarah_support: will DM you the throttler snippet and a short doc on API key management (automation via /v1/keys). sample throttler (JS):```js
// simple token-bucket naive
let tokens = 100; // refill rate matched to plan
setInterval(()=> tokens = Math.min(tokens+1, 100), 1000);
async function callApi(req){
  while(tokens<=0) await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, 200));
  tokens--;
  return fetch(req);
}
```
alex_cust: perfect. thanks. last ask — we saw one 401 a bit after the bridge was applied, maybe a stale worker. can you keep the bridge running until tomorrow morning PST?
ben_sales: we can extend once if needed. open to extending to 48h, but will need a short postmortem email from you confirming mitigation steps and next steps to avoid repeat.
alex_cust: yes can do. we'll send the postmortem and switch to per-worker keys tonight. thanks everyone. :party_parrot:
sarah_support: closing loop — bridge set to expire 24h from application, ben put a note to extend if we get your postmortem by end of day tomorrow. feel free to reopen thread if anything else pops up.
